title: Policy-gated firmware trust and anti-rollback resilience for autonomous UAV edge platforms (Scientific Reports, 2026)
page_numbers: Physical PDF page numbers (same as the page_label PyPDFLoader returns for this file).
how_to_score: q01-q25: hand-grade against ground_truth. u01-u05: pass only if the answer says I don't know.

questions.question: Which standard does the paper cite as separating protection, detection and recovery of platform firmware?
questions.ground_truth: NIST SP 800-193.

questions.question: What two critical weaknesses did the study find in the original firmware-admission mechanism?
questions.ground_truth: It accepted inadequately verified integrity metadata when a required secret was absent, and it accepted a candidate even when preserving the previously trusted state failed.

questions.question: Which language, compiler and test framework were used for the experiments?
questions.ground_truth: A native C++20 build using GCC on Linux and the CTest framework.

questions.question: What stored record, and what version-only and counter-only candidates, does the test plan use?
questions.ground_truth: Accepted record with version 2.1.0 and rollback counter 4; the version-only candidate uses 2.0.5 with the counter unchanged; the counter-only candidate uses counter 3 with the version unchanged.

questions.question: Which fields of the candidate firmware manifest are listed in Table 1?
questions.ground_truth: Firmware version, measurement, signer, integrity field, secure-boot claim, bootloader-lock claim and rollback counter.

questions.question: How is the manifest integrity field computed, and is it an HMAC?
questions.ground_truth: SHA3-256 over a newline-delimited concatenation of the secret and selected manifest fields; it is not an HMAC, a digital signature or verified secure-boot evidence.

questions.question: Which status does the hardened implementation return when the accepted-state record cannot be written?
questions.ground_truth: STATE_PERSISTENCE_FAILED.

questions.question: What does the maintenance gate actually check?
questions.ground_truth: Only whether the maintenance token is non-empty when maintenance mode is on; an empty token gives MAINTENANCE_UNAUTHORIZED and any non-empty token passes the presence check.

questions.question: Which measurement strings does the measurement predicate reject?
questions.ground_truth: Empty measurements and development-marked strings such as unsigned and lab-local.

questions.question: Which signer identifiers does the application supply by default, and are they proof of a certificate chain?
questions.ground_truth: release-ca and maint-ca; they are only textual policy entries and not evidence of a certificate chain or protected signing key.

questions.question: How does the version comparator work, and is it a full Semantic Versioning implementation?
questions.ground_truth: It compares dot-separated integer components in order, so 2.1.0 is newer than 2.0.5 and equal versions are allowed; it is not a complete Semantic Versioning implementation.

questions.question: When is a candidate rejected by the anti-rollback gate, and are the two checks independent?
questions.ground_truth: It is rejected when either the version or the rollback counter regresses, irrespective of the other; the two checks are independent.

questions.question: What are the three trusted computing assumptions A1, A2 and A3?
questions.ground_truth: A1: the startup executable and validator are not modified or bypassed (secret stays non-empty); A2: the profile, signer list, secret, manifest source and prior record are protected; A3: boot claims come from a separately trusted source.

questions.question: What happens if an attacker restores an older state file?
questions.ground_truth: An obsolete firmware image can pass the local comparisons against the restored file, so software file storage alone does not give durable rollback resistance.

questions.question: What measurement value does the application set in hardened profiles when none is supplied?
questions.ground_truth: The marker unsigned-local-build, which the hardened measurement predicate denies.

questions.question: After each rejection, what does the test fixture compare, and what must be true?
questions.ground_truth: It compares the complete stored acceptance record byte-for-byte with its baseline; the state file must remain unchanged.

questions.question: What recovery design does the paper suggest for future work?
questions.ground_truth: An A/B firmware layout with a known-good recovery image, where recovery itself must satisfy an authenticated manifest policy.

questions.question: What three tracks of future work are named?
questions.ground_truth: (i) move integrity verification to asymmetric signed manifests; (ii) replace external boot claims and file-based counters with hardware-backed evidence and monotonic state; (iii) integrate recovery and remote attestation.

questions.question: Which generative AI tool was used and for what tasks?
questions.ground_truth: ChatGPT, to assist with language drafting, mathematical presentation and document formatting.

questions.question: What was the first weakness found in the original admission code, and which status does the hardened version now return for it?
questions.ground_truth: The original code accepted a nonempty integrity field when no signing secret was set; hardened profiles now return TRUST_CONFIGURATION_INVALID.

questions.question: Does a non-empty maintenance token switch off the other firmware checks, and is the token itself authenticated?
questions.ground_truth: No: boot, rollback, signer, digest and measurement checks still apply; the token is not authenticated and any non-empty token passes the presence check.
evidence: does not bypass the other predicates

questions.question: How many firmware-specific tests were there, and does the count of 273 mean 273 separate attack experiments?
questions.ground_truth: The firmware-specific results are 3 original tests plus 17 added cases; the 273 count is the whole native suite, not 273 separate firmware-attack experiments.

questions.question: How many original firmware trust tests existed before the 17 added cases?
questions.ground_truth: Three: a trusted production configuration, a combined version/counter rollback and maintenance without a token.

questions.question: Which status is returned in hardened profiles when secure_boot_attested is false?
questions.ground_truth: SECURE_BOOT_FAILED.

questions.question: Which status does a candidate from a signer that is not on the allowlist get?
questions.ground_truth: SIGNER_REJECTED.
